verdict.rationale: Buzz's relay is a WebSocket server that third-party Nostr clients connect to directly with NIP-29/NIP-42 authentication, which works as a gateway-style real-time connection. Bots get their own keypairs. The first-party buzz-acp harness shows a bot listening for @mentions on the relay in real time and replying. missing for 10: explicit documentation of event subscription and filtering semantics (which event kinds a bot can subscribe to and how), a dedicated bot developer guide, and independent hands-on corroboration of building a custom bot on the relay connection.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a bot that receives messages and events in real time through an events API or gateway connection

citations.quote: Third-party Nostr clients connect directly to `buzz-relay` using NIP-29 and NIP-42 authentication.
The harness listens for @mentions on the relay, prompts your agent, and the agent replies using the Buzz CLI.
buzz-relay # WebSocket relay server — main entry point; also hosts git + huddle audio
Each agent needs a Nostr keypair — this is the agent's identity in Buzz
